race_context: The Metropolitan School District (MSD) of Decatur Township serves Decatur Township on the southwest side of Marion County (Indianapolis) and enrolled roughly 6,500 students last year {cb_dec_guide} {cb_dec_times}. Chalkbeat reported in 2024 that nearly 72% of students come from low-income households {cb_dec_2024}. The superintendent is Scott Collins, who started in July 2024 after leading Fayette County Schools {cb_dec_2024} {cb_dec_times}.
The board has five members, all elected at large by voters throughout the district {cb_dec_guide} {cb_dec_2024}.

Seat count: three at-large seats are on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot, and the top three vote-getters win; new members serve through 2030 {cb_dec_guide} {wfyi_results_2022}. The state candidate list shows this race as "vote for 1"; reporting indicates voters choose three {in_list} {cb_dec_guide}.

Incumbents: the three seats are held by Judith Collins, Dale Henson and Chase Lyday, all Republicans seeking reelection; Chalkbeat reported that Collins and Henson have each served about two decades and Lyday since 2023 {cb_dec_guide}. The other two members, Larry Taylor and Estella Vandeventer, were reelected unopposed in 2024 to terms through 2028 {cb_dec_2024}. A Mirror Indy Documenters agency page lists Henson as board president, Lyday as vice president and Collins as secretary {documenters}.

Field: eight candidates, the second-largest field in Marion County: four with no party, three Republicans and one independent {cb_dec_guide} {cb_overview}. School board races are not part of straight-ticket voting {cb_overview}.

Budget and property taxes: district leaders anticipated $3 million less in property taxes in 2026 because of the state's 2025 property tax changes {cb_dec_times}. In June 2026 the district announced new school start and end times, moving from six bell schedules to three to cut bus routes and save on a roughly $6.7 million transportation budget; more than 70% of students ride the bus daily {cb_dec_times}.

Referendum: the board placed an operating referendum on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot that would repeal the levy voters approved in 2019 and replace it with a new eight-year levy of up to $0.2690 per $100 of assessed value (maximum $9 million a year) for student transportation, utilities, school safety and security, building maintenance and support services. The state-approved ballot language says the tax bill on a median $250,000 home would increase by $306 a year if approved {dlgf_dec}. The current rate is roughly 29 cents {cb_dec_times}; Chalkbeat described the measure as replacing the existing rate with a lower one, while still a tax increase from the base amount through 2034 {cb_dec_guide}. Superintendent Collins said without referendum funds the district would have to consider busing changes such as walk zones and cutting after-school buses {cb_dec_times}.
State law passed in 2026 requires public school districts to share more property tax revenue with charter schools, which Chalkbeat reported could make referendums harder to pass {cb_takeaways}.

Forums: no 2026 candidate forum for this district was found. The Chalkbeat Indiana / Mirror Indy / WFYI survey published Sept. 11, 2026 is the main source of candidate positions; Teresa A. Burns, Judith Collins, Steve Jacobi and Kristyn D. Stoddard did not respond to it {cb_dec_guide}.

Points of difference among survey respondents: Berryman, Henson and Lyday said they support the referendum, while Johnson said it deserves careful consideration rather than a yes-or-no answer; Berryman raised concerns about the new school start times, while Henson and Lyday cited the change as a cost saving; Berryman named academic underperformance relative to neighboring districts as the top issue, while Henson and Lyday emphasized literacy and funding pressures {cb_dec_guide}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent board member since 2023, running as a Republican; former police chief for Avon Community Schools {cb_dec_guide}.
background: Age 39; graduated from Decatur Central High School and attended Ivy Tech Community College; has no children in the district {cb_dec_guide}.
Previously served as police chief for Avon Community Schools {cb_dec_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as a Republican {in_list} {cb_dec_guide}.
Won his seat in 2022 as "Steven Chase Lyday" by a single vote, 2,540 to 2,539, over Jimmy Ray for the third at-large seat; no recount was requested {wfyi_results_2022}.

items: Supports the referendum, saying it is needed to continue services such as mental health support, school resource officers and child nutrition workers {cb_dec_guide}.

Listed solidifying fiscal plans in light of the deficit created by tax code changes as a priority, and wants data to drive spending decisions and more outside grants and local partnerships {cb_dec_guide}.
Lists continuing a comprehensive approach to school safety as a top priority {cb_dec_guide}.
Wants substantial resources focused on early elementary students reading at grade level and passing IREAD, and literacy resources for older students {cb_dec_guide}.
Called taking care of teachers and funding literacy specialists, mental health counselors, school resource officers and coaches the most pressing issue {cb_dec_guide}.
Said he meets community members for coffee and lunch, takes calls at all hours, and routes concerns to administrators and follows up {cb_dec_guide}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. Said the district has done "an excellent job" saving money and executing an efficient spending plan {cb_dec_guide}.
plans: Pass the referendum, continue the safety program, raise early literacy scores and pursue grants and partnerships {cb_dec_guide}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found; fundraising is unknown.
No campaign website was found.
No record of his individual board votes was reviewed. The board officer roles listed on the Documenters page are undated.

candidates.summary: Incumbent board member for about two decades, running as a Republican; retired Decatur Township fire chief {cb_dec_guide}.
background: Age 69; graduate of Decatur Central High School and the National Fire Academy; does not have children in district schools {cb_dec_guide}.
Retired as Decatur Township's fire chief in 2014 after 35 years, and was executive director of the Indiana Fire Chiefs Association {cb_dec_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as a Republican {in_list} {cb_dec_guide}.
Reelected in 2022 with 2,899 votes, second among four candidates for three seats {wfyi_results_2022}.

items: Supports the referendum, citing legislative changes to school funding and a $3 million reduction in 2026 {cb_dec_guide}.
Said the new start times will cut fuel costs, and that Decatur was the only Marion County school corporation to reduce its total 2026 budget, by half a million dollars {cb_dec_guide}.
Goals: keep the graduation rate at 95% or higher (he cited 97.48% in 2025), meet the state average on IREAD-3 with a goal of 95%, and raise ILEARN language arts and math scores by 3% {cb_dec_guide}.
Called reading the district's top academic focus {cb_dec_guide}.
Listed being safety-conscious for students and staff among the most pressing issues {cb_dec_guide}.
Said he has always been open to listening to community members and attends many district events besides monthly meetings {cb_dec_guide}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. Cites the 2025 graduation rate, the 2026 budget reduction and the start-time change as evidence of the board's fiscal responsibility {cb_dec_guide}.
plans: Meet stated graduation, IREAD and ILEARN targets and pass the referendum {cb_dec_guide}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found; fundraising is unknown.
No campaign website was found.
A Ballotpedia page for "Dale Henson" appeared in search results but was not reviewed.

candidates.summary: Community service provider and district parent running with no party affiliation {cb_dec_guide}.
background: Age 36; holds a bachelor of science in public health education and works as a community service provider {cb_dec_guide}.
Her daughter graduated from Decatur Central High School; her son attends school online {cb_dec_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan {in_list} {cb_dec_guide}.

items: Said the referendum "deserves thoughtful consideration rather than a simple yes or no answer," and that taxpayers should know why more money is requested, how it would be spent, what accountability would apply and what alternatives were explored {cb_dec_guide}.

Proposed reviewing operating expenses, contracts and vendor agreements, pursuing grants and partnerships, and aligning programs with measurable outcomes before asking taxpayers for more {cb_dec_guide}.
Wants to strengthen reading and math, use achievement data to identify struggling students, and support advanced coursework {cb_dec_guide}.
Lists transparency as a top priority; said the district must rebuild trust and explain why decisions are made, and plans regular communication through events and social media {cb_dec_guide}.

on_incumbent: Called rebuilding trust while balancing financial pressures one of the district's biggest challenges, saying families want to know why decisions are made {cb_dec_guide}.
plans: Review spending and contracts, hold the district accountable for measurable results, and communicate regularly with families {cb_dec_guide}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found; fundraising is unknown.
No coverage beyond the Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey was found; her campaign Facebook page could not be reviewed.

candidates.summary: Scientist running with no party affiliation, focused on academic performance and budget review {cb_dec_guide}.
background: Age 42; holds a bachelor of science degree and works as a scientist {cb_dec_guide}.
Has a child who does not attend a district school {cb_dec_guide}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state candidate list as Nonpartisan {in_list} {cb_dec_guide}.

items: Called underperformance the district's most pressing issue, saying Decatur is falling behind neighboring districts; wants to focus on math, science and language arts and review curriculum against top-performing districts {cb_dec_guide}.
Supports the referendum, but said funding must be paired with a clear plan for how dollars improve student outcomes and teacher salaries {cb_dec_guide}.
Would conduct a budget review across departments, compare spending with other districts, and scrutinize administrative overhead and vendor contracts {cb_dec_guide}.
Plans regular listening sessions, input channels for parents, teachers, staff and students, and public reporting back {cb_dec_guide}.

on_incumbent: Expressed "serious concerns" about the district's new school start times, citing research on age-appropriate schedules and student health {cb_dec_guide}.
plans: Budget analysis and reallocation toward classrooms, curriculum review, and data-driven decision-making {cb_dec_guide}.
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found; fundraising is unknown.
No campaign website or coverage beyond the Chalkbeat/Mirror Indy/WFYI survey was found.
